clue.text: Composer's loose end

definitions.meaning: Maurice ..., the French composer of Bolero
a tangle or a loose thread end that has come undone

explanation.definitionFit: One sense names the French composer; the other is an old noun for a frayed or tangled thread.

clue.text: Nice English dress fashionable for Government Houses

indicators.note: fashionable is read as fashioned, shaped into a new arrangement of letters

explanation.surface: A smart English dress worn in Nice for an occasion at Government House.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city in the surface but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Government Houses are the official homes of colonial governors.

clue.text: Vehicle going in or out after service

definitions.meaning: a road vehicle for goods

definitions.text: going in or out after service
definitions.meaning: in tennis, ... is short for advantage, called '... in' or '... out' after deuce

explanation.surface: A vehicle driving in or out after its service at the garage.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is tennis: after deuce the score is advantage, shortened to 'van in' or 'van out' depending on whether server or receiver leads.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a goods vehicle and also the tennis abbreviation of advantage.

clue.text: Shoots birds

definitions.meaning: in gardening, a stem pegged down to root while attached to the parent plant
hens kept for eggs

explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners root stems pegged into soil; egg-producing hens are also so called.

clue.text: Carnage Marat found himself in

definitions.meaning: carnage is a massacre, a slaughter with much blood spilt
the revolutionary Jean-Paul Marat was stabbed to death in his bath, so it literally filled with blood

explanation.surface: A historical note on where the French revolutionary Marat met a bloody end.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: Marat was murdered by Charlotte Corday while sitting in his bath, which turned to blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A massacre is figuratively a bath of blood, and Marat's was a literal one.

clue.text: One goes behind the scenes to assist the clergy

parts.note: to back someone is to support or assist them
the cloth means the clergy collectively

explanation.surface: A volunteer working behind the scenes to help the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind the scenes' is literal: a painted curtain hung at the rear of a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted curtain hung at the rear of a stage forms the scenery's backdrop.

clue.text: Get the better of non-ruling party

parts.note: a party not in power is out
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: An opposition party trying to beat the government.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass or beat someone is to excel them.

clue.text: One trusted to move rubbish

indicators.note: to move tells us the letters are shifted into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A trusted person asked to move some rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris and waste fragments are a kind of litter or refuse.

clue.text: Everyone, for example, finds Coral Island curiously symbolic

parts.note: everyone means all

indicators.note: curiously means the letters come out oddly, in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Everybody finds Ballantyne's novel Coral Island strangely full of symbolism.
explanation.walkthrough: The Coral Island is a Victorian adventure novel, but here 'Coral' and the I from 'Island' are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory conveys hidden meanings through symbols, so the adjective means symbolic.

clue.text: Pay attention to something the editor includes

indicators.note: includes tells us the letters sit within the words the editor

explanation.surface: A request to pay attention to something the editor has put in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something' is a link word: the letters come from inside 'the editor'.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed is to take notice of or listen to advice.

clue.text: Vessel that needs an onshore wind

definitions.text: Vessel that needs an onshore wind

parts.words: Vessel that needs an onshore wind
parts.note: a vessel sounds like a boat at sea, but this sailing craft runs on wheels over a beach, so it wants wind blowing over the shore rather than out at sea

explanation.definitionFit: A wheeled sailing craft raced along beaches is pushed by breezes across the shoreline.

clue.text: Implement, say, for dressmaker

indicators.note: say tells us to take the word as it is spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: an implement is a tool

explanation.surface: A dressmaker reaching for the right implement.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a fine netted fabric, something used by a dressmaker, just as a tool is.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine silk net is a fabric a dressmaker works with for veils and ballet skirts.

clue.text: Probate? It's needed for those lost at sea

definitions.meaning: probate settles the estate of someone deceased, whimsically an accounting of the departed

definitions.text: It's needed for those lost at sea
definitions.meaning: navigators who have lost their position calculate it from speed, heading and time elapsed

explanation.surface: A legal process somehow related to sailors lost at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Probate is read whimsically as a reckoning for the dead; the real phrase is the navigator's method of estimating position without landmarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Navigators estimate position from course and speed; probate, jokily, is a reckoning for someone deceased.

clue.text: Object to secondary head's lack of purpose

parts.note: an object is an aim or goal
less, as in lesser, means minor or secondary
a ness is a headland; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Someone objecting that the deputy head lacks purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' is a headland, NESS, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Drifting without a goal is having no direction.

clue.text: Evaluation intended in hearing, starting with Jenny?

indicators.note: starting with puts the jenny piece at the front

parts.note: a jenny is a she-ass, and the question mark hints at the possessive ass's, whose sound is spelt ASSESS

indicators.note: in hearing tells us the word for intended is taken as it would be heard, not spelt

parts.note: intended means meant

explanation.surface: A test of what was meant, beginning with someone called Jenny.
explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, 'ass's meant' gives the answer; 'Jenny' is not a girl but a female donkey, and 'in hearing' turns MEANT into MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is an appraisal or judgment of worth.

clue.text: Handle fame

definitions.meaning: a handle is slang for what someone is called
to make a ... for oneself is to win renown

explanation.definitionFit: Both a slang term for what one is called and a word for renown, as in making one's mark.

clue.text: They produce sweet airs in musical medleys

definitions.meaning: bowls of dried scented petals give a room a pleasant fragrance
the word also means a medley of tunes strung together

explanation.surface: A description of musical medleys full of sweet tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airs' looks musical, but the first sense is about scents in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried petal mixtures scent a room; the same word means a miscellany of melodies.

clue.text: Origin of a tear in leaf of book

indicators.note: in tells us the a and tear pieces go within the leaf

parts.note: a leaf of a book is a page
a rent is a tear or rip

explanation.surface: Where a tear in a page of a book came from.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lineage or descent is the source one comes from.

clue.text: Taking part as usual in nature project

parts.note: type means kind or nature
to cast is to throw or project

explanation.surface: Someone joining a nature project as they always do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' is an acting role: an actor always given the same kind of role.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor always given the same kind of role is stuck in a stock part.

clue.text: Funnily, her very wee lamb accompanied Mary thus

indicators.note: funnily suggests the words are arranged in an odd way, so their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A whimsical retelling of the nursery rhyme about Mary's very small lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme runs 'Everywhere that Mary went, the lamb was sure to go'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme the lamb followed Mary to every place she went.

clue.text: A measure for port

definitions.meaning: a unit of land area, 4,840 square yards
a seaport city of that name in northern Israel, famed for its crusader walls

explanation.surface: Someone asking for a measure of port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests the fortified wine served in measures; it is a harbour town in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a unit of land area and also the name of a Mediterranean harbour city in Israel.

clue.text: Man, possibly? Not according to the poet

definitions.meaning: the Isle of Man is one example of a piece of land surrounded by sea
John Donne wrote 'No man is an ...'

explanation.surface: A question whether a man is something, answered with a poet's denial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man, a self-governing island in the Irish Sea. Donne's line 'No man is an island' supplies the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is surrounded by sea, and Donne denied that any man was so cut off.

clue.text: They may bring people round to see sailors humming

parts.note: humming is British slang for stinking, giving off an odour
salts, as in old salts, are sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors who smell so bad they bring people round to see them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humming' is British slang for smelly. 'Bring round' means revive from a faint.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammonia-based restoratives are held under the nose to revive someone who has fainted.

clue.text: Master left to get money

parts.note: to earn is to get money by working

explanation.surface: A master leaving a job to make money.
explanation.definitionFit: To master a skill is to acquire it fully by study.

clue.text: Find fault before parking vehicle

indicators.note: before places the parking piece after the vehicle, so the vehicle comes first

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone complaining before parking their car.
explanation.definitionFit: To complain or nitpick about trivial things is to cavil.

clue.text: Bowl in America in sports centre

definitions.meaning: in the US a bowl is a stadium, as in the Rose Bowl
a stadium or ring where contests are held

explanation.surface: Someone going bowling at an American sports centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowl' looks like the game of bowls; the American sense is a stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: An American stadium is called a bowl, and a stadium is a venue for sport.

clue.text: See man in pain in landslide

indicators.note: in tells us the see and man pieces sit inside the word for pain

parts.note: an ache is a pain
V is the abbreviation of Latin vide, see
Alan is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man in agony caught in a landslide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' gives V from Latin vide, used in references.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of snow or rock sliding down a mountain is much like a landslip.

clue.text: A fair one makes a justifiable arrest

definitions.text: A fair one makes a justifiable arrest

parts.words: A fair one makes a justifiable arrest
parts.note: the criminal's admission on being caught, 'it's a fair one', names a policeman's nab that is justified; fair also tempts us towards a fair-haired person

explanation.definitionFit: The slang noun for an arrest appears in the phrase admitting one was rightly caught.

clue.text: Over-anxious? It could be perfect

parts.note: over means finished, gone by
anxious means nervy, on edge

explanation.surface: Someone over-anxious about being perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perfect' is a grammatical term here: the perfect is one form of the verb for completed time.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the perfect is one kind of verb form referring to completed actions.

clue.text: Hit the bottle on the way back to headquarters

indicators.note: on the way back means the word for drinking is read from its end to its start

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily, so hit the bottle in the past is toped

explanation.surface: Someone drinking heavily while returning to headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' is past tense, so the drinking verb is TOPED, which 'on the way back' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a military base or regimental headquarters.
